01-graph: The cube and the 22-vertex running graph G, with faces labelled. Filled vertices are black, hollow vertices white. The bold edge is e0. Face labels use the shared dual layout, but only edges of G are drawn.
02-pair: A pair as incidence matchings: blue solid segments assign s; vermilion outlined segments assign r. Endpoints labelled f are primal faces, not vertices of G. Each nonroot black vertex and each nonroot face occurs once in each colour.
03-disk: Green halos mark the vertices inside the cut side S; dashed vermilion edges form its boundary. The four counts below each graph satisfy (4.2). On the right h=7 and ell=2; the cut side has five black and six white vertices. Inside means the shore missing b0.
04-flow: Integer path flow from b0 to every white vertex of G. Arrows show net direction; labels give absolute flow. Every white vertex absorbs one unit. For the positive circuit orientation the weight is the number of white vertices in S, equivalently the white faces of T. Blue flow arrows are independent of the dashed cut orientation.
05-cancellation: The same second state s and its two partners. Dashed primal edges are Q_s, viewed as links between faces. Reversing the tails on its odd face circuit exchanges the outlined incidence segments and reverses the sign. The blue state, and hence its entire weight polynomial, stays fixed.
06-recovery: The recovered perfect matching P is bold black; G-P is the purple Hamiltonian cycle. Every vertex has one matching edge and two cycle edges, and e0 belongs to P. Both objects are computed from the parent edges of the recovery tree.
07-cut: A nontrivial three-edge cut in the glued-cube example, dashed vermilion. Its two capped shores are the cube pieces shown next. This example is separate from the irreducible running graph.
08-pieces: The two capped pieces of the preceding cut, both cubes. The cap vertices replace the opposite shores. Deleting the cap vertices from compatible Hamiltonian cycles gives two spanning paths that glue across the two retained cut edges.
